subject: Flexible launch commit + tiered accelerator proposal
content:
From: Alex Park <alex@launchpad.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring monthly commit ladder for big Q4 launch

Hi Jonas,

We're ramping toward a major product launch in early November and evaluating hosted API partners. Our usage will be heavily skewed for the first 8 weeks of launch, then settle into a steady monthly run-rate. Looking for guidance on structuring a monthly commit that: 1) lets us start small, 2) ramps up automatically during launch weeks, and 3) provides meaningful per-token discounts as we hit tiers.

Key context: initial expected peak is ~1.2B tokens in Nov week 1, then 400–600M tokens/mo after 3 months. We also need a short-term burst allowance without committing to a much higher baseline.

Can Redwood support a step-up commit (monthly true-up) + a temporary surge buffer? What does pricing look like if we want granular per-token discounts (e.g., 10M increments) versus broader tiers?

Thanks,
Alex Park
Head of Product, Launchpad AI
alex@launchpad.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Park <alex@launchpad.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring monthly commit ladder for big Q4 launch

Hi Alex — great to meet (virtually). Thanks for the context. Short answer: yes, we can design a monthly commit structure that supports an initial low baseline, a step-up ramp, and a temporary surge buffer with a defined true-up. Below is a concise proposal to start the conversation. I attached a sample commit schedule that maps to your launch profile.

Attachment: Commit_Schedule_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 54KB)

Proposal (high level)
- Baseline commit: 300M tokens/mo for months 1–2 (discount tier A).
- Launch ramp: automatic step-up to 800M tokens/mo in month 3 (tier B) if usage crosses defined trigger threshold in preceding month.
- Temporary surge buffer: additional 500M tokens available for 30 days at a discounted premium (buffer price = baseline per-token * 1.2) to avoid throttling during launch spikes.
- Monthly true-up: reconciliation monthly with overage billed at the effective per-token rate for the tier achieved during that month; we offer a cap on overage cost during the first 90 days of launch.
- Granularity: we can do finer-grained discounts in 25M increments — 10M increments are possible but add complexity to billing and reporting; recommend 25M for balance of flexibility and ops simplicity.

Next steps
1) If this structure looks directionally right, Marissa (cc'd) will draft a quote and propose exact per-token prices by tier and the surge buffer fee.
2) We can add a seasonality clause to allow temporary step-downs for predictable low-traffic months.
3) If legal needs specific language for the true-up or surge buffer, loop in your counsel and we can circulate redlines.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to talk numbers.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood-inference.com

From: Alex Park <alex@launchpad.ai>

Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring monthly commit ladder for big Q4 launch

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick reply and the outline — helpful. A couple clarifying Qs before we schedule the call: 1) For the surge buffer, can that be pre-reserved (so we get capacity guarantees) or is it best-effort with a price premium? 2) For true-up billing, do you reconcile by calendar month or by rolling 30-day windows? That matters for us because our usage will be concentrated in a 10–14 day burst.

Also, this will likely be a two-contract conversation: procurement for the service + a separate SLA addendum for our enterprise customers. Do you have standard language for short-term buffer guarantees? If so please share.

Appreciate it — Alex

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Park <alex@launchpad.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Sep 2025 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Exploring monthly commit ladder for big Q4 launch

Alex — looping in pricing/finance here. Per your questions:

1) Surge buffer: we can offer a pre-reserved surge buffer (capacity guaranteed) as part of a short-term addendum. Two options:
   - Guaranteed buffer (reserved capacity): fixed monthly fee + per-token usage at buffer rate. Guarantees latency/throughput during buffer windows.
   - Best-effort buffer: no reservation fee, higher per-token premium, no hard SLA on capacity.

2) Reconciliation window: we reconcile on a calendar-month basis by default. For launch scenarios concentrated in 10–14 day windows, we can provide a one-time rolling-30-day true-up for the first invoice period to avoid split-month distortions.

3) Pricing granularity: we recommend 25M token increments for tier thresholds. Sample pricing (illustrative):
   - Tier A (0–300M): $0.000120 per token
   - Tier B (300M–800M): $0.000095 per token
   - Tier C (800M+): $0.000072 per token
   - Surge buffer rate: 1.20x Tier achieved rate for buffer consumption

4) Governance / legal: we have a standard "Buffer Addendum" that defines reservation, billing, and a limited SLA for the reserved buffer (uptime commitment during buffer windows). I attached a draft quote and the sample commit schedule.

Attachments: Redwood-Launch-Accelerator-Quote-v2.pdf (pdf, 120KB); Commit_Schedule_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 54KB)

We can also include an optional clause for a 3-month ramp discount that phases down after month 3 if you fall below agreed run-rate.

If that looks good, I'll put together a formal quote and DocuSign envelope for signatures.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood-inference.com
